briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan's market shrinks under the 24% tax — as psilocybin nears an FDA first
briefs.top: Michigan just posted its first-ever annual cannabis sales drop as the new 24% wholesale tax forces closures and layoffs statewide. Nationally, rescheduling cleared a key hurdle and Compass' psilocybin is closing in on the first FDA-approved psychedelic therapy.

local.text: Michigan's weed market is shrinking for the first time — 2025 sales fell to $3.17B (from $3.27B), with 550+ dispensaries and growers closed since 2019 as the 24% tax lands.
Ann Arbor's C3 Industries is closing its 35,000 sq ft Webberville grow and cutting 62 jobs — the CEO says the model isn't sustainable under the new tax.
Higher Love, a U.P. dispensary chain, laid off 61 people — about 28% of its staff across 9 stores — bracing for the tax hike.
The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's suit to kill the 24% tax — arguing it needed a three-quarters legislative vote — is still moving through the Court of Claims.
Even Ann Arbor's cut is shrinking: the city expects ~$1.2M in cannabis tax revenue this year — about $200K less than last — as sales slump.

national.text: Cannabis rescheduling cleared a key procedural milestone Aug 18 — a proposed rule is expected by December, public comment in Q1 2027, and a final Schedule III rule by mid-2027.
The federal hemp-THC ban still hits Nov 12 absent new law (~95% of hemp products go unlawful) — now the wine & spirits lobby is pushing to regulate THC drinks instead of banning them.
Psilocybin is at the FDA's door: Compass' COMP360 hit its primary endpoint in TWO Phase 3 trials — a U.S. first for a classic psychedelic — with an approval call expected late 2026 or early 2027.
FDA 'priority vouchers' to Compass, Usona & Transcend can compress review from ~12 months to 1-2, on top of Trump's April order accelerating psychedelic approvals.
Mark the calendar: the FDA holds a public hearing on the therapeutic use of psychedelics on Sept 14.
